newsitem.title: JORDAN: Cement stocks push Jordan market down for 3rd day.
newsitem.headline: Cement stocks push Jordan market down for 3rd day.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell for a third consecutive day on Tuesday in moderate trade, driven down by a fall in heavily-traded bluechip Jordan Cement Factory.
Jordan Cement fell 0.02 dinars to 4.02 dinars in trade worth 170,000 dinars ($242,000) despite some buying from overseas investors, brokers said.
It helped drag the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index down 0.16 percent to 159.00 points in turnover of 707,000 dinars.
"Trading is still weak," said broker Husam al-Hanbali.
The official index has eased this month after gaining nearly six percent in the final week of May on the back of foreign fund buying.

Shares in Jordan National Bank rose 0.05 dinars to 2.11 dinars, backed by both foreign and local demand, while buying from local investors boosted trade in Housing Bank stock to around 100,000 dinars.
Jordan Kuwait Bank, which delayed an extraordinary general meeting planned for Friday until next month, rose 0.06 dinars to 3.27 dinars in trade worth 34,000 dinars.
Brokers say a tussle for boardroom control of the bank, linked to a possible takeover by Bank of Jordan, has stimulated trading this week.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers on Tuesday by 19 to 10, with another nine trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.11 percent to 81.50 points, 2.27 percent down from the start of the year.
